title: Quantitative live-cell imaging of Candida albicans escape from immune phagocytes
protocol: Observe seeded macrophages using a light microscope.
Stain macrophage membranes with CellTracker Green.
Infect macrophages with C. albicans at MOIs of 1:1 and 3:1 (C. albicans:macrophage).
Allow phagocytosis to occur.
Add CFW and DRAQ7 to the medium to detect escaped C. albicans hyphae and permeabilized macrophages, respectively.
Replace the culture medium of macrophages with 100 μL per well of FBS-free BMDM differentiation medium containing 1 μM CellTracker Green CMFDA dye.
Incubate the macrophages at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 30 min.
Vortex mix BMDM differentiation medium for at least 10 seconds.
Replace the macrophage medium with infection medium, 100 μl per well.
Centrifuge the microplates containing infected BMDMs at 500 x g for 3 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Incubate the infected BMDMs at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 1.5 hours to allow phagocytosis.
Rinse each well with 150 μl of sterile PBS three times to remove unphagocytozed C. albicans cells.
Add imaging culture medium containing DRAQ7 and CFW to each well.
Proceed immediately to the live cell imaging step after permeabilizing BMDM membranes and staining with CFW if necessary.
Mount the 96-well microplate on a stage inside a microscopy incubator set to maintain cells at 37°C and 5% CO2 for live cell imaging.
Ensure the microscope incubation chamber is pre-heated to 37°C, with CO2 supplied at 5%, ahead of image acquisition.
Mount the 96-well plate to the microscopy stage.
Seal the microscope incubator.
Set up imaging positions within the 96-well microplate.
Program two positions for image acquisition within each well.
Save the position information file in a convenient location.
Acquire images of CellTracker Green fluorescence for all imaging positions.
Set up a channel that captures CellTracker Green fluorescence using a FITC filter cube.
Set up a second autofocus channel using either bright-field or far red (Y5 filter cube) for autofocus.
Preview image acquisition for each channel and optimize illumination settings accordingly.
Adjust illumination settings to acquire images of lower brightness, prioritizing cell viability.
Capture CellTracker Green fluorescence for all positions and save the image file.
Acquire C. albicans hyphal escape images at 30 min intervals for 18–24 hours.
Set up a bright-field channel.
Set up channels for DRAQ7 fluorescence capture.
Set up channels for dTomato fluorescence capture.
Set up channels for CFW fluorescence capture.
Preview image acquisition settings for each channel.
Check autofocus settings using the DRAQ7 fluorescence channel.
Specify time intervals for image acquisition.
Start live cell image acquisition.
Observe image acquisition during the entirety of the first time point.
Ensure each image is in focus.
Verify that image collection within each time point occurs within the specified timeframe.
Generate illumination-correction images for image analysis.
Use captured live cell images in the C. albicans hyphal escape image analysis pipeline.
Correct for image vignetting using media-only controls.
Remove vignetting from an image of escaping (CFW-stained) hyphae using the “ImageMath” module in CellProfiler.
Select images of empty wells for each channel.
Open at least four empty well images in ImageJ per channel.
Produce a median projection image using the selected empty well images.
In ImageJ, click on "Image," then select "Stacks" and choose "Images to stack."
Click "OK" when prompted to combine the selected images into a single stack.
Select "Z project" from the "Stacks" menu in ImageJ.
Perform a median projection of the image stack.
Click "OK" to proceed.
Apply a Gaussian blur effect using the "Process" menu, followed by selecting "Filters," then "Gaussian Blur."
Set the radius to 16 and confirm your choice by clicking "OK."
Locate the maximum intensity value in the image using the "Analyze" menu, select "Set measurements," ensure that "min & max gray value" is checked, and click "OK."
Measure the maximum intensity value.
Note the maximum intensity value obtained for subsequent calculations.
Normalize the intensity values of the image by selecting "Process" menu, then "Math," choose "Divide," enter the previously noted maximum value, and confirm the settings.
Save this normalized image by going to the "File" menu, select "Save as," and choose the TIF format.
Provide an appropriate name, such as "IllumCor" followed by the month and year.
Repeat Steps 15–20 for each channel (CFW, DRAQ7, dTomato and CellTracker Green).
Use illumination correction images generated within the same experiment.
Avoid using outdated or different microscope illumination correction images.
Quantify the total number of macrophages (permeabilized and viable).
Quantify the area of phagocytozed and escaped C. albicans.
Use image analysis software CellProfiler for measurements.
Provide settings and notes on image analysis modules in supplementary tables.
Perform analysis A.
Use CellTracker Green staining to quantify the total number of macrophages in the field of view at the first time point.
Apply the CellProfiler project settings provided in Table S1 and S2 for this step.
Import all CellTracker Green (“CtG”) images into the "Images" module by dragging and dropping the files into the window.
Check that each .TIF file name contains information about the position, time point, and channel.
In the metadata module, check that channel, position, time series, and image type information are captured for all images.
In the NamesAndTypes module, check that each CellTracker Green image is listed next to the same illumination correction image.
Select the eye icon next to the ImageMath and IdentifyPrimaryObject modules to be “open”.
Select “Start Test Mode” in the bottom left corner of the program interface.
Select “Step” to progress through the image analysis modules.
To progress through all image analysis modules, select “Run”.
Segment macrophages from each treatment condition within an experiment.
Optimize the segmentation using images from each treatment condition.
Validate segmentation of all images.
Select “Exit Test Mode” after validation.
Adjust cell thresholding and segmentation parameters as necessary for optimal results.
Adjust cell segmentation parameters, including object diameter and thresholding value, for optimal segmentation results.
Validate image analysis settings by ensuring single macrophages are correctly segmented and avoiding multiple segmentations of the same cell.
Select “Press to select measurements” to confirm that the correct measurements are set to be exported in ExportToSpreadsheet module.
Nominate a destination folder for export of the spreadsheet file under “Output file location.”
Save the finalized project file in a location separate from the template file.
Press “Analyze Images” to begin analysis.
Deselect the “eye” icons next to the analysis modules for faster processing.
Perform analysis B using DRAQ7 staining to quantify permeabilized macrophages over time.
Drag-and-drop all hyphal escape analysis TIF image files into the “Images” module.
Include the DRAQ7 illumination correction image in the analysis.
In the Metadata module, check that hyphal escape assay images are of “hea” type.
Check that the illumination correction image appears as “None”.
List each DRAQ7 image (“hea”, channel 0) alongside the same illumination correction image in the “NamesAndTypes” module.
Test all cell segmentation parameters.
Adjust the expected object diameter accordingly in the “IdentifyPrimaryObjects” module for DRAQ7-positive nuclei.
Prepare the export of data.
Save the project file.
Run the analysis as described.
Perform analysis C.
Quantify the total area of dTomato and CFW-positive C. albicans.
Correct vignetting in images before thresholding and area measurements occur.
Add TIF “hea” images to the “Images” module.
Add two illumination correction images to correct vignetting for both dTomato and CFW images.
Check that the regular expression extracts relevant metadata from image file names in the “Metadata” module.
Assign channel identifiers to the dTomato and CFW images using the “NamesAndTypes” module.
Prepare the export of data.
Save the project file.
Run the analysis as described in Step 22g-j.
